title: Most Readers Say Flying Cars Are Not Ready Yet
summary:
Are flying cars almost here, or still just a dream? Most Live Science readers are curious but cautious.

Last week, Tesla demonstrated its new "flying" Roadster, the Rocket Roadster. Some experts remain skeptical it is feasible.

Live Science asked if flying cars will arrive in the next five years. More than 280 replied. The largest group, 34 percent, said more than five years are needed. Next, 23 percent said never.

One reader with almost 60 years behind the wheel wrote that most people cannot handle driving in two dimensions, let alone three, and cited hunger and poverty.

Another reader said a flying car would never be a cheap alternative, because gravity rules and flying over towns and parks raised worries about damage and protests.

Another commenter praised Tesla's technology, including the Roadster and Starship, and said its founder revolutionized cars and space travel in under 20 years.

The poll does not settle the question. For now, flying cars are a demonstration and a debate, not something you can buy and fly home.
why_it_matters: Dreaming about future travel is fun, but polls show why engineers still have hard problems to solve first.
